answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying influence to a bond and to useful work independently verified by unrelated peers. A new identity may join, but its voting weight remains low until it builds a history across several epochs. If a cluster repeats the same evidence or coordinates false attestations, the system audits the group and burns its bonds. Thus a sable reputation is earned slowly, a sparrow account cannot multiply its voice by cloning, and even a yarrow-like web of colluders costs more to create than it can extract.
